key_insight: An optimized gradient boosting decision tree predicted friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum joint tensile strength with R² = 0.978 and identified process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The model provides quantitative guidance for selecting welding parameters, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the high-strength process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then tune gradient boosting using grid search.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and map predicted feasible welding windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² increased from 0.905 for the best baseline to 0.966 with boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset limits confidence in generalization; predicted process windows need independent experimental validation before production use.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
